meta.reader: an ML engineer on X who runs and debugs LLM agents; knows sampling and tool calls; has never met Forking Paths Analysis or forkscope
meta.contradicts: the reader believes a failed transcript shows its mistake somewhere, and that high-entropy tokens mark the decisive step; here the fatal step looks clean and is found only by replaying futures
meta.source: forkscope-report.md + data/reports/replay_t4_*.json (Qwen3-8B, SGLang deterministic inference, Chinook DB)
meta.spine_rejected: instrument-pipeline diagram (trajectory in, resampler, o_d out): teaches the architecture, not the phenomenon; the reader learns to read the instrument faster by watching it applied to one real failing run

sections.asks: What does one agent run hide?
sections.shows: the real t4 run as a two-step path: question, one SQL tool call returning 1, a confident wrong answer; at each decision step, ghost branches the sampler could have taken fade off the path

instead_of.because: a process chain shows the steps taken; the claim is the untaken branches, which only a drawing can put beside the path

sections.asks: How does forkscope measure one decision step?
sections.shows: the prefix frozen at step d, K=50 full continuations fanning out, every tool call really executed, endpoints binned by final answer into a tally: that tally is o_d

instead_of.because: the mechanism is one simultaneous fan, not an accumulation of parts

sections.shows: o_d as stacked tallies at d=0 and d=1: mixed (22% correct / 58% integer-division / 20% other) collapsing to a single bin after the first SQL, both directions shown, 1.00 on the AVG path and 0.00 on the COUNT/COUNT path

instead_of.because: two share bars carry the proportions but not the collapse between them, which is the finding
